The '''2022 World Championship''' was the 27th Star Wars CCG World Championship, held by the [[Players Committee]] in Atlanta, Georgia, over the weekend of 14–16 October 2022, with four sanctioned events across three days.<ref name="wrap" /> (The hub previously gave 13–16 October.) The main event had 51 players.<ref name="wrap" /> [[Justin Desai]] defeated [[Matthew Harrison-Trainor]] in the Final Confrontation with Moment Of Triumph (V) and The Galaxy May Need A Legend,<ref name="wrap" /><ref name="pc">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2022-swccg-world-championship/ 2022 SWCCG World Championship], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/2022-swccg-world-championship.html swccg.com snapshot]</ref> winning his third World Championship (after 2013 and 2015) and joining [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] as the only three-time champions.<ref name="wrap" />

=== Top 8 bracket ===

[[Joe Olson]] was the only player at 7–1 after Day 1. Nine players finished 6–2, in order: Desai, [[Ryan Jellison]], [[Greg Shaw]], [[Kyle Krueger]], [[Hayes Hunter]], Harrison-Trainor, [[Jeremy DiPaolo]], [[Chris Wirfs]] and [[Sam Tashima]]. In two play-in games DiPaolo beat Wirfs and Harrison-Trainor beat Tashima.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Quarterfinals:''' Desai def. Krueger; Harrison-Trainor def. Shaw.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Semifinals:''' Desai def. Hunter; Harrison-Trainor def. Olson.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Final:''' Desai def. Harrison-Trainor.<ref name="wrap" />

The other two quarterfinal results and all game scores were not published.

== Side events ==

* '''Team tournament''' (Friday evening, 12 teams, glass mug trophies): won by [[Justin Desai]] and [[Steve Baroni]] ("Kashyyyk Train of Dominance"); [[Matthew Harrison-Trainor]] and [[Matt Lutz]] ("Drs. Matt") were second. [[Dan Tartaglione]] directed the event.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Consolation''' (Sunday): won by [[Jonny Chu]] at 5–1; [[Ryan Sersen]] was second. [[Bill Kafer]] directed the event.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Throdo's Cube Spectacular''' (Friday, draft and four games, 28 players): won by [[Phil Aasen]] ahead of teammate [[Cal Aldred]]; organized by [[Jonathan Murray]].<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Main-event teams:''' players were assigned to teams for an "event within the event" based on main event performance.<ref name="wrap" />
